newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: New Zealand's Maori queen launches new warship.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand's Maori queen launches new warship.

text.p: New Zealand's Maori queen on Saturday launched a new warship for the nation's navy in a ceremony that ignored lingering criticism of the Australian-built frigate as a waste of money.

Australian and New Zealand prime ministers joined thousands of onlookers, including senior Australian and New Zealand naval officers, to cram a dry dock here on Australia's Port Phillip Bay to watch the Te Mana roll down the slipway.
"May God bless her and all who sail in her," said Te Arikinui Dame Te Atairangikaahu before bringing a champagne bottle down onto the ship's bow with an embarrassing bounce.
It smashed on the second attempt.

The ANZAC-class frigate, the second of two built for the Royal New Zealand Navy at a total cost of about NZ$1.2 billion (US$816 million), has been called a waste of money by some New Zealanders who believe the ships serve no strategic purpose.
New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger skirted the criticism, but said the new frigate, with a range of 6,000 nautical miles, would do more than help ensure regional security in the Pacific.
The Te Mana will also be used to protect New Zealand's fisheries, come to the aid of the country's cyclone-devastated island neighbours and rescue seamen in distress, Bolger said.

New Zealand has an option to buy two more of the ANZAC frigates, at a cost of less than NZ$500 million each, for delivery around years 2004-2005, Captain Alan Peck, of Royal New Zealand Navy, told Reuters at the Williamstown shipyard.
The option expires in November, Peck said.
New Zealand is preparing to make decisions from late this year on the future equipment needs of the country's entire defence force up to the year 2010, said Bolger.
"It is during this period the core assets of the New Zealand defence force, that have served New Zealanders' needs for many years, come to the end of their operating life," he said.
The frigate Te Mana, which loosely translates from Maori as "power", is an empty shell which still needs to be fitted out.
In two years, when it is finally delivered, it will carry a missile system, torpedo tubes and a crew of 164.
